steps.instructions: Verify whether the underlying reprocessing cycle completed successfully and whether the issue is limited to documentation or export. Expected outcome: A cycle-processing problem is not mistaken for a record-transfer problem.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Barcode Scanner and External Accessories
steps.instructions: Check the scanner cable, connector, power state, scanning window, and physical condition. Test a known-readable barcode if available. Expected outcome: The scanner reads and transfers data normally. If a loose connection or dirty scanner window was responsible, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Printer Supplies and Connections
steps.instructions: If printing is affected, verify approved paper or media is installed correctly, the printer is not jammed, covers are closed, and accessible cables or connections are secure. Expected outcome: The printer accepts media and produces a complete readable record. If corrected, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Review Record Availability at the AER
steps.instructions: Determine whether the completed cycle record is present locally even when it did not print or export. Do not delete or overwrite useful records during troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to output or transmission rather than cycle-record creation.

steps.title: 7. Inspect External Network or Tracking Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible Ethernet, USB, serial, or other approved external connections used by the facility. Look for disconnected, damaged, or loose cables and verify applicable network indicators. Expected outcome: Physical connectivity is intact. If reconnecting an approved external cable restores export, troubleshooting can stop after a test record.

steps.title: 8. Compare Local Versus Infrastructure Failure
steps.instructions: If possible, determine whether other AERs or connected devices can communicate with the same tracking system or network service. Expected outcome: A facility-wide tracking or network outage is separated from a single AEROFLEX fault.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Documentation Test
steps.instructions: Generate or use an approved test workflow to confirm barcode entry, local record creation, printing, and export as applicable. Expected outcome: Required cycle documentation is correctly recorded and delivered to its intended destination.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Documentation Failure
steps.instructions: If local records, peripherals, cables, and external infrastructure appear normal but required output still fails, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is escalated to ASP service, IT, interface support, or the tracking-system vendor as appropriate.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported completed AEROFLEX cycles were recorded locally but were not exporting to the tracking system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network cable partially disconnected at the reprocessor.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the cable, verified normal link indication, and confirmed a subsequent cycle record exported successfully.

helpfulDetails: Function affected: barcode, printer, local record, or export

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) AEROFLEX Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Endoscope Leak Test or Channel Flow Verification Fails
description: Leak-test or channel-flow failures caused by scope damage, incorrect connections, tubing problems, blocked channels, adapters, or reprocessor-side connection issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Endoscope and Patient Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not continue automated processing of an endoscope that fails a required leak test or channel verification. Remove the affected scope from the workflow and provide another verified scope if clinically needed. Expected outcome: A potentially damaged or inadequately processed endoscope is not returned to service.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Verification Is Failing
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported problem is a leak-test failure, one specific channel failing flow verification, multiple channels failing, or the entire verification sequence not starting. Expected outcome: The affected function and channel are clearly identified. If the reported problem cannot be reproduced and all required checks pass, continue to final verification before returning the system to service.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Endoscope Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect the scope for visible damage, fluid intrusion concerns, damaged connectors, cracked components, loose caps, or other obvious abnormalities. Do not continue using a scope with suspected integrity damage. Expected outcome: The scope is externally intact. If damage is found, remove the scope from service and do not use the AER to compensate for the scope defect.

steps.title: 4. Verify Correct Scope Connections and Adapters
steps.instructions: Confirm all required channel connectors, tubing, adapters, and leak-test connections are appropriate for the endoscope and are fully seated. Look for crossed, loose, omitted, kinked, or incorrectly routed tubing. Expected outcome: Every required connection is secure and correctly routed. If correcting the connection restores verification, troubleshooting can stop after a successful cycle check.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Tubing and Connector Condition
steps.instructions: Check accessible tubing and fittings for splits, kinks, pinching, blockage, debris, worn seals, or damaged locking features. Expected outcome: Tubing remains open and connections remain sealed. Replace approved damaged external accessories as appropriate and repeat verification.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Endoscope or Connection Set
steps.instructions: When facility workflow allows, determine whether the failure follows the endoscope or remains with the AER position by using a compatible known-good scope or approved connection set. Expected outcome: If the failure follows one scope, remove that scope from service for endoscope evaluation. If multiple known-good scopes fail at the same AER position, continue troubleshooting the reprocessor.

steps.title: 7. Check Basin Loading and Scope Positioning
steps.instructions: Verify the endoscope is loaded without sharply bent insertion tubing, compressed channels, trapped connectors, or tubing positioned where the lid can pinch it. Expected outcome: The endoscope and tubing remain freely positioned throughout the verification process. If repositioning restores normal flow verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Repeat Verification Under Controlled Conditions
steps.instructions: Run the required verification again with known-good external connections and observe whether the same channel or leak-test failure repeats. Expected outcome: The leak test and all required channel checks pass consistently. If they do, proceed to final functional verification.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Repeated Failures
steps.instructions: If known-good scopes and connection sets produce the same failure, stop external troubleshooting. Do not bypass channel verification or leak testing. Expected outcome: The affected AEROFLEX is removed from service pending qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported repeated channel-flow verification failure on the same AEROFLEX basin.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found one channel-connection tube kinked beneath the endoscope during loading.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the tubing routing, repeated channel verification successfully, and confirmed normal operation with the approved setup.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) AEROFLEX Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Lid/Door Will Not Lock or Reports Open During the Cycle
description: Lid or door interlock problems caused by obstruction, loading, damaged seals, alignment, latch contamination, or failed position detection.

steps.title: 1. Protect Personnel and Processing Safety
steps.instructions: Do not bypass, defeat, tape, hold, or otherwise override a lid or door interlock. Stop processing and use another validated reprocessor if needed. Expected outcome: The AER remains unable to run unless the enclosure is safely secured and recognized.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the lid or door physically will not close, closes but will not lock, unlocks unexpectedly, or remains displayed as open during a cycle. Expected outcome: Mechanical closure and electronic recognition are distinguished.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Obstructions
steps.instructions: Check the basin edge, door or lid path, latch area, and sealing surface for tubing, endoscope components, labels, packaging, debris, or other material preventing full closure. Expected outcome: The lid or door closes freely without interference. If removing an obstruction restores normal locking, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Endoscope and Tubing Loading
steps.instructions: Verify no connector, hose, scope segment, or accessory extends into the closure path. Expected outcome: The load remains entirely within the intended processing area and does not interfere with the enclosure.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Seals and Accessible Latch Surfaces
steps.instructions: Look for displaced, folded, contaminated, damaged, or swollen seals and inspect accessible latch surfaces for residue or damage. Expected outcome: The sealing and latching areas are clean, intact, and correctly positioned. Do not operate the unit with visibly damaged safety-related closure components.

steps.title: 6. Operate the Lid or Door Without a Load
steps.instructions: With the basin empty and the device otherwise ready, check whether the enclosure closes and is recognized normally. Expected outcome: If the problem disappears without a load, loading or tubing placement was likely responsible. If it remains, continue.

steps.title: 7. Check for Intermittent Recognition
steps.instructions: Without forcing the mechanism, observe whether normal gentle closure consistently changes the displayed status from open to closed. Expected outcome: Recognition is stable. Intermittent or position-sensitive recognition suggests a service-level interlock or alignment problem.

steps.title: 8. Verify Normal Cycle Initiation After Correction
steps.instructions: After correcting an external issue, perform an approved test and verify the lid or door remains properly locked and recognized throughout the required portion of the cycle. Expected outcome: The enclosure remains secure and no false open indication occurs. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Interlock Failure
steps.instructions: If the enclosure is unobstructed and properly aligned externally but still will not lock or is reported open, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The unit is removed from service rather than operated with an unreliable safety interlock.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the AEROFLEX lid would close but continued to display open and would not start the cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a channel hose trapped along the basin edge and preventing full lid closure.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned the hose, verified normal lid recognition and locking, and completed an approved operational cycle test successfully.

helpfulDetails: Physically open versus electronically reported open

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) AEROFLEX Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Water Filter, Water-Quality Test, or Final-Rinse Condition Fails
description: Water-related processing failures involving external supply, filter condition, installation, water-quality verification, inadequate flow, or unacceptable final-rinse conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Reprocessing Safety
steps.instructions: Do not release endoscopes processed when required water-quality or final-rinse conditions are not verified. Use an alternate validated reprocessing workflow. Expected outcome: No scope is returned to patient use after an uncertain rinse or water-quality condition.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Water-Related Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves a filter warning, failed water-quality test, poor fill performance, final-rinse failure, or repeated cycle abort associated with water supply. Expected outcome: The water problem is narrowed to supply, filtration, testing, or processing.

steps.title: 3. Check Facility Water Availability
steps.instructions: Verify the water supply to the AEROFLEX is available and that accessible shutoff valves are in their normal operating position. Ask whether plumbing or facility work recently occurred. Expected outcome: Normal facility water is available to the unit. A closed valve or facility outage is corrected before further testing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Supply Hoses and Connections
steps.instructions: Look for kinks, pinching, leaks, loose fittings, or obvious damage in accessible water-supply hoses. Expected outcome: Water can reach the AER without external restriction or leakage. If correcting a hose issue restores operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Water Filter Installation
steps.instructions: Check whether the approved filter is correctly installed and whether accessible filter housings or connections show leakage, improper seating, or obvious contamination. Expected outcome: The filter system is correctly assembled and leak-free. Correct installation problems and repeat the required check.

steps.title: 6. Review Filter Status and Replacement History
steps.instructions: Determine whether staff recently replaced a filter or whether the failure began immediately after filter service. Do not invent or override replacement intervals. Expected outcome: A newly introduced installation issue is identified if present. If proper approved filter replacement resolves the condition, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Repeat the Approved Water-Quality Verification
steps.instructions: Using the facility's approved test method and applicable manufacturer instructions, repeat the required water-quality check. Do not substitute unapproved test methods. Expected outcome: Water quality meets the required pass condition. If it does not, investigate facility water or filtration rather than repeatedly processing scopes.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Facility Water Conditions
steps.instructions: If appropriate, determine whether other equipment supplied by the same water source is showing similar problems or whether facilities has identified a supply-quality issue. Expected outcome: A building-side water problem is separated from an AEROFLEX-specific problem.

steps.title: 9. Verify Final-Rinse Operation After Correction
steps.instructions: Perform an approved operational test and confirm the AER fills, rinses, drains, and completes the required final-rinse stage normally. Expected outcome: Final-rinse operation and required water checks pass. The device may return to service after all required verification is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Water Failures
steps.instructions: If supply, hoses, filter installation, and facility water have been ruled out, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The AEROFLEX is removed from service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the AEROFLEX repeatedly failed the water-quality check after a filter change.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the replacement water filter was not fully seated in its housing.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the approved filter installation, repeated the required water check successfully, and verified normal final-rinse operation.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - ALLClear Barcode or Cycle-Record Export Fails
description: Troubleshoot barcode, cycle-record, or tracking export failures involving scanners, labels, connections, network infrastructure, configuration, or receiving systems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Traceability and Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: If required cycle documentation or traceability cannot be maintained, follow facility policy before continuing routine instrument processing. Do not treat successful sterilization and successful record export as the same function. Expected outcome: Sterilization records remain traceable through an approved alternate workflow while the interface issue is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Define the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Barcode not scanning Barcode data not populating Cycle record created locally but not exported Missing patient, load, or instrument information Intermittent transmission Complete loss of connectivity Expected outcome: The local scanner, sterilizer record, and external export functions are separated into distinct test points.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Barcode and Scanner
steps.instructions: For barcode-related complaints, inspect: Label condition Print clarity Barcode damage Scanner window Scanner cable and connector Scanner positioning Test more than one known-good barcode when available. Expected outcome: The scanner reads a known-good barcode reliably. If it does, the original label or barcode is the likely cause.

steps.title: 4. Check External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect all accessible communication connections associated with the affected workflow. Look for: Loose connectors Damaged cables Bent or damaged plugs Disconnected network cable Unintended connection changes Do not alter protected network infrastructure or internal wiring. Expected outcome: All required external connections are secure and undamaged.

steps.title: 5. Verify Local Cycle Record Creation
steps.instructions: Determine whether the STERRAD NX itself generates and retains the expected cycle information. If the record exists locally but is missing from the external system, focus troubleshooting on communication or integration rather than sterilization performance. Expected outcome: Local record creation is confirmed independently from export.

steps.title: 6. Verify User-Accessible Communication Status
steps.instructions: Review available operator-accessible network or communication indications without changing protected configuration. Compare with known facility records when available. Expected outcome: The sterilizer shows its expected communication status and no unauthorized configuration changes are made.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Other Systems
steps.instructions: Determine whether: Other STERRAD systems can export records The receiving tracking system is online The problem affects only one sterilizer The problem began after network or software changes Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to the STERRAD NX, network path, or receiving application.

steps.title: 8. Test With Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: Where appropriate and approved, substitute a known-good external scanner or communication cable of the correct type. Expected outcome: The function returns with the substitute component, identifying an external accessory or cable problem. Troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 9. Verify Complete Data Flow
steps.instructions: After correction, confirm the entire workflow: Barcode or identifier → STERRAD NX record → completed cycle record → intended receiving or tracking system. Expected outcome: The correct record reaches the intended destination and is associated with the correct cycle.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Communication Failures
steps.instructions: If local record creation works but export remains unavailable, engage the appropriate ASP service, IT, integration, or tracking-system support team based on where the failure was isolated. Expected outcome: The device is not subjected to unnecessary internal repair when the problem lies in external infrastructure.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that STERRAD NX cycle records were completing locally but were not appearing in the tracking system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network connection to the sterilizer was loose while local cycle-record generation remained normal.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the external network connection, verified successful cycle-record transmission to the tracking system, and returned the interface to service.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Cassette Is Rejected, Will Not Index, or Reports No Cycles Remaining
description: Troubleshoot cassette rejection, indexing problems, recognition failures, or cycle-availability messages caused by cassette condition, installation, consumables, or system readiness.

steps.title: 1. Protect Sterile Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a STERRAD NX that cannot reliably recognize or advance the sterilant cassette. Redirect loads to another validated sterilization process or verified sterilizer according to facility procedures. Do not repeatedly attempt processing of instruments while cassette status is uncertain. Expected outcome: Required instrument processing continues using verified equipment while the affected sterilizer is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Cassette Complaint
steps.instructions: Record the displayed message and determine whether the cassette: Is rejected immediately Is accepted but will not index Indicates no usable cycles remain Becomes unavailable during cycle setup Was functioning normally before the current event Do not assume the cassette or sterilizer has failed based only on a general report such as "cassette problem." Expected outcome: The failure point and displayed condition are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Cassette Externally
steps.instructions: Using appropriate PPE and facility procedures for handling the sterilant cassette, inspect it for: Physical damage Leakage or contamination Distortion Improper storage or handling Obvious signs that it should not be used Do not attempt to open, modify, refill, or repair the cassette. Expected outcome: The cassette is intact and suitable for installation. If damaged or leaking, remove it from use and stop troubleshooting with that cassette.

steps.title: 4. Verify Correct Cassette Installation
steps.instructions: Remove and reinstall the cassette only according to approved operating procedures. Confirm it is fully seated in the intended orientation and that nothing externally obstructs its insertion or movement. Do not force the cassette or cassette mechanism. Expected outcome: The cassette installs normally without binding or excessive force.

steps.title: 5. Check Cassette Status and Consumable Availability
steps.instructions: Verify that the installed cassette is appropriate for the STERRAD NX and has remaining usable capacity according to the system indication and facility inventory controls. If the system correctly identifies an exhausted cassette, replace it with an approved cassette. Expected outcome: A usable cassette is installed and recognized with available processing capacity. If normal operation returns, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Test With a Known-Good Approved Cassette
steps.instructions: When permitted by facility procedures, substitute another properly stored, undamaged, approved cassette. Do not repeatedly sacrifice consumables if multiple known-good cassettes are rejected. Expected outcome: A known-good cassette is recognized and indexes normally. If it does, remove the original cassette from use and document the finding.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Accessible Cassette Loading Area
steps.instructions: With the sterilizer idle and safe to inspect, check the externally accessible cassette-loading area for: Packaging debris Obvious obstruction Damage Contamination Misalignment visible without disassembly Do not reach into inaccessible mechanisms or defeat covers or interlocks. Expected outcome: The loading path is clean and unobstructed with no obvious external damage.

steps.title: 8. Restart Only When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If no cycle is active and facility procedures permit, perform a normal shutdown and restart to determine whether the cassette recognition interface recovers. Do not use repeated power cycling to bypass a persistent cassette fault. Expected outcome: The sterilizer starts normally and recognizes an approved cassette. If cassette handling remains reliable through setup, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before returning the sterilizer to service, verify: Normal startup Cassette recognition Normal cassette status indication Successful cycle setup No recurring cassette-related message Any facility-required functional or quality checks Expected outcome: Cassette operation is repeatable and the sterilizer is suitable for return to service.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Cassette-System Problems
steps.instructions: If multiple known-good cassettes are rejected, the cassette will not index, or the mechanism shows abnormal operation, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The sterilizer is removed from clinical processing pending qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD NX repeatedly rejected the installed sterilant cassette and would not proceed to cycle setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the installed cassette was not recognized, while a known-good approved cassette was accepted and indexed normally.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the suspect cassette from use, installed a known-good cassette, verified normal cassette recognition and cycle setup, and returned the sterilizer to service after required checks.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Chamber Door Will Not Lock, Seal, or Release After a Cycle
description: Troubleshoot door locking, sealing, or release problems caused by obstruction, load placement, debris, power state, cycle status, or service-level door mechanisms.

steps.title: 1. Protect Personnel and the Load
steps.instructions: Do not force the chamber door, defeat the interlock, or attempt to open a chamber that the sterilizer has not released. If a cycle did not complete normally, treat the load as unprocessed until handled according to facility and manufacturer procedures. Expected outcome: Personnel remain protected and the load is not incorrectly released for clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Door Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the door: Will not close Closes but will not lock Reports open when physically closed Will not seal Remains locked after cycle completion Became stuck following an aborted cycle or power event Expected outcome: The failure is defined before physical intervention.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for External Obstruction
steps.instructions: With the sterilizer safe to inspect, check the doorway for: Packaging material Tray edges Instruments extending beyond the load area Debris Foreign material Visible contamination Expected outcome: Nothing interferes with normal door movement or sealing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Door and Seal Areas
steps.instructions: Visually inspect accessible surfaces for: Debris Damage Distortion Residue Obvious seal displacement Do not remove or adjust internal door components unless authorized by service documentation. Expected outcome: The accessible door and sealing surfaces are clean and appear intact.

steps.title: 5. Verify Load Position
steps.instructions: Confirm that trays and packages are fully inside the chamber and are not contacting the door or preventing closure. Expected outcome: The load does not interfere with door operation.

steps.title: 6. Check Cycle and System Status
steps.instructions: Review the displayed system state. A door may remain locked while the system is completing a controlled phase, recovering from a cancellation, or maintaining a safety condition. Do not interrupt the system solely to release the door unless directed by approved procedures. Expected outcome: The displayed status explains normal temporary locking, or confirms an abnormal persistent condition.

steps.title: 7. Verify Power Stability
steps.instructions: If the complaint followed a power interruption, verify normal AC power and allow the sterilizer to complete its approved startup or recovery process. Do not repeatedly remove power to force door release. Expected outcome: Normal power and control operation are restored and the door releases or locks appropriately.

steps.title: 8. Test Door Operation Without a Clinical Load
steps.instructions: When the sterilizer is safe, idle, and authorized for testing, check whether the door closes and the system recognizes it normally without a clinical load. Expected outcome: Door status changes correctly and the system proceeds through normal setup. If so, the previous load or obstruction was likely responsible.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting an external cause, verify: Normal door closing Correct lock indication No abnormal movement Normal cycle initiation Proper release at the end of an approved verification cycle Expected outcome: Door operation is repeatable throughout the complete cycle. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Door or Interlock Problems
steps.instructions: If the door remains locked unexpectedly, will not secure reliably, or gives incorrect status with no obstruction present, remove the sterilizer from service. Expected outcome: Door, latch, interlock, seal, or control-system evaluation is performed by qualified service personnel.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD NX chamber door would close but would not lock for cycle initiation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a section of packaging material trapped at the chamber opening and interfering with complete closure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the obstruction, inspected the accessible door area, verified normal locking and release through an approved test cycle, and returned the sterilizer to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether issue followed a canceled cycle

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Chamber or Load Temperature Is Outside the Permitted Range
description: Troubleshoot temperature-related processing problems caused by load conditioning, room environment, recent instrument processing, placement, chamber condition, or temperature-control faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Sterility Assurance
steps.instructions: Do not release a load from a canceled or invalidated cycle associated with an unacceptable temperature condition. Move time-sensitive instrument processing to another validated system. Expected outcome: Patient instruments are not released from a cycle with questionable processing conditions.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Temperature-Related Condition
steps.instructions: Document: Complete displayed message Whether the issue concerns the chamber or load When in the cycle it occurs Instruments involved Whether the condition repeats with every load Do not assume a failed temperature sensor without first evaluating load and environment. Expected outcome: The problem is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Evaluate Recent Load History
steps.instructions: Determine whether instruments were recently: Washed Heated Removed from another processing system Stored in a cold area Transported between substantially different environments Coordinate corrective handling with Sterile Processing. Expected outcome: The load has been appropriately conditioned before processing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect for Moisture and Condensation
steps.instructions: Check the load for: Visible water Condensation Damp packaging Moisture retained in channels or complex devices Temperature and moisture problems may occur together. Expected outcome: The load is visibly dry.

steps.title: 5. Verify Load Arrangement
steps.instructions: Confirm trays and packages are positioned correctly and are not crowded, stacked improperly, or contacting the chamber in an unusual manner. Expected outcome: The load is appropriately arranged.

steps.title: 6. Check the Chamber Condition
steps.instructions: With the sterilizer idle and safe, inspect the accessible chamber for: Moisture Debris Unusual residue Foreign material Expected outcome: The chamber is clean and dry.

steps.title: 7. Check the Room Environment
steps.instructions: Determine whether HVAC failure, room-temperature changes, sterilizer relocation, or prolonged shutdown could have affected the equipment or loads. Do not adjust manufacturer calibration or temperature settings as an external troubleshooting step. Expected outcome: No facility environmental condition explains the problem.

steps.title: 8. Compare With a Properly Conditioned Known-Good Load
steps.instructions: When permitted, process an approved test or controlled load that is dry and at normal room conditions. Expected outcome: The controlled load processes successfully. If so, the original load condition was responsible and equipment troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Verify Successful Processing
steps.instructions: After correcting the external condition, complete the required cycle and quality verification. Expected outcome: The cycle completes without temperature-related cancellation and all required records and indicators are acceptable.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated Temperature Faults
steps.instructions: If correctly prepared and conditioned loads continue to trigger temperature faults, remove the sterilizer from service. Expected outcome: Qualified service evaluates temperature sensing, chamber conditioning, controls, or related systems.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported repeated STERRAD NX load-temperature cancellations with instruments brought directly from another processing area.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the problem followed recently heated loads while a properly conditioned control load processed normally.
CCR.Resolution: Coordinated appropriate load conditioning with Sterile Processing, verified a successful cycle with a properly prepared load, and returned the sterilizer to routine service.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Moisture Detection or Load-Temperature Cancellation Repeats
description: Troubleshoot recurring moisture or load-temperature cancellations caused by wet instruments, packaging, load preparation, room conditions, recent equipment use, or sterilizer problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Sterility Assurance
steps.instructions: Do not release any load from a canceled cycle. Move processing to another validated sterilizer or approved process while investigating repeated cancellations. Expected outcome: No potentially unsterile instrument is released for patient care.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Cancellation Condition
steps.instructions: Document the complete displayed message and determine whether the system reports: Moisture Load temperature Both under different circumstances The condition only with specific trays or instruments Expected outcome: The reported condition is distinguished from a general cycle cancellation.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Load for Moisture
steps.instructions: Coordinate with Sterile Processing to inspect instruments and packaging for: Residual rinse water Moisture in lumens or channels Wet tray surfaces Damp wraps or pouches Condensation Recently washed equipment that has not adequately dried Expected outcome: The load is visibly dry before processing. If moisture is found, correct the preparation problem before further testing.

steps.title: 4. Review Load Preparation and Timing
steps.instructions: Determine whether the affected devices were: Recently washed Recently removed from another heat-producing process Stored in a cold location Brought directly from a substantially different environment Packaged before drying was complete Do not modify validated processing procedures; coordinate process corrections with Sterile Processing leadership. Expected outcome: Instruments are prepared and conditioned appropriately for the intended STERRAD process.

steps.title: 5. Check Load Arrangement
steps.instructions: Verify that the chamber is not overloaded and that packages, trays, and devices are positioned according to approved processing practices without crowding or contact that could trap moisture. Expected outcome: The load is arranged appropriately with no obvious external condition likely to interfere with processing.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Chamber
steps.instructions: With the sterilizer safe and idle, check the accessible chamber for: Residual moisture Debris Spilled material Packaging fragments Unusual condensation Do not disassemble chamber components. Expected outcome: The chamber is clean and dry.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Dry Load
steps.instructions: When permitted, run an approved test or controlled dry load. If only specific instruments or load configurations trigger the cancellation, the problem likely follows the load rather than the sterilizer. Expected outcome: A known-good dry load processes normally. If so, stop equipment troubleshooting and address the load-preparation issue.

steps.title: 8. Check Room and Equipment Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify there has not been an unusual environmental event such as: Significant room temperature change HVAC problem Sterilizer relocation Prolonged shutdown Condensation-producing conditions Expected outcome: The sterilizer and loads are operating under normal facility environmental conditions.

steps.title: 9. Verify Repeatable Successful Processing
steps.instructions: After correcting an external cause, complete the facility-required verification cycle and review the cycle record. Expected outcome: The cycle completes without moisture or temperature cancellation. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Unexplained Repeated Cancellations
steps.instructions: If known-good dry and appropriately conditioned loads continue to produce the same cancellation, remove the sterilizer from service. Expected outcome: Qualified service personnel evaluate the sensing, vacuum, chamber-conditioning, control, or related systems.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported repeated STERRAD NX moisture cancellations with a recently washed instrument load.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found residual moisture in the load while a controlled dry load processed normally.
CCR.Resolution: Coordinated proper drying and reprocessing of the affected instruments, verified successful operation with a dry load, and returned the sterilizer to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether moisture or temperature was reported

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Printer Feeds but the Cycle Record Is Blank or Incomplete
description: Troubleshoot blank, faint, partial, or incomplete cycle printouts caused by paper installation, paper type, obstruction, printer condition, or data-generation problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Cycle Documentation
steps.instructions: Do not discard electronic or other available cycle documentation while troubleshooting the printer. If printed records are required by facility policy, establish an approved alternate documentation method before continued routine processing. Expected outcome: Sterilization traceability is maintained despite the printer problem.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Printing Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the printer: Feeds blank paper Prints only part of the record Produces faint output Stops before the record is complete Fails only for certain cycles Produces no printed information despite paper movement Expected outcome: Paper-feed and print-generation problems are distinguished.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Paper Installation
steps.instructions: Verify that the approved paper is: Present Loaded correctly Oriented correctly Not wrinkled or damaged Feeding through the intended path Do not force paper into the mechanism. Expected outcome: Paper is correctly loaded and moves normally.

steps.title: 4. Verify Paper Type
steps.instructions: Confirm the installed paper is the correct approved type for the printer. A printer may feed normally but produce blank output if inappropriate media is installed. Expected outcome: Correct printer media is installed. If replacing incorrect paper restores printing, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Accessible Paper Path
steps.instructions: Check for: Torn paper Adhesive residue Debris Misaligned roll Obvious obstruction Do not disassemble the printer mechanism beyond authorized user-accessible areas. Expected outcome: The accessible paper path is clear.

steps.title: 6. Compare Printed and Electronic Cycle Information
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complete cycle record exists on the sterilizer display or electronic record system. If complete data exists electronically but the printed copy is incomplete, the problem is localized toward printing rather than cycle-record generation. Expected outcome: Record-generation and physical-printing functions are isolated.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Test Print or Cycle Record Print
steps.instructions: Use available normal printer functions to generate a record where permitted. Observe paper movement and print quality. Expected outcome: The printer produces a complete readable record.

steps.title: 8. Check for Intermittent Behavior
steps.instructions: Print more than one approved record if necessary to determine whether the fault is repeatable. Do not declare the problem corrected based on a single partial improvement. Expected outcome: Printing remains consistent across repeated use.

steps.title: 9. Verify Documentation Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm that: Complete cycle information is present Print is readable Required identifiers are included Records can be retained according to facility policy Expected outcome: Normal cycle documentation is restored and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Printer Problems
steps.instructions: If correct paper is installed and the paper path is clear but records remain blank or incomplete, remove the printer function or sterilizer from use as required by facility documentation policy and escalate for service. Expected outcome: Qualified service evaluates the printer or record-generation system.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD NX printer advanced paper but every cycle record came out blank.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an incorrect paper roll installed while electronic cycle records remained complete.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the paper with the approved type, verified multiple readable cycle-record prints, and returned the printer function to service.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Sterilizer Will Not Power On or Unexpectedly Restarts Mid-Cycle
description: Troubleshoot no-power and unexpected restart complaints caused by facility power, cords, connections, external protection devices, environmental conditions, or internal power faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Load and Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: If the STERRAD NX loses power or restarts during a cycle, consider that cycle unsuccessful unless system documentation and facility policy specifically establish otherwise. Do not release the affected load for patient use. Redirect processing to another validated sterilizer. Expected outcome: The interrupted load remains controlled and patient care continues using verified equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Power Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The unit is completely dead The display briefly illuminates It powers on and shuts off It restarts only during a cycle Other equipment on the same circuit was affected The event followed a facility power disturbance Record the cycle phase if a restart occurred during processing. Expected outcome: A no-power condition is distinguished from intermittent reset or facility power loss.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the External Power Connection
steps.instructions: Check the accessible power cord, plug, and connection for: Loose connection Damage Heat discoloration Cracked insulation Bent or damaged plug components Evidence of liquid contamination Do not use a damaged power cord. Expected outcome: The external power connection is secure and undamaged.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Facility Power Source
steps.instructions: Using appropriate Clinical Engineering or Facilities procedures, verify that the intended receptacle has power. If appropriate, compare with another known working outlet or test using approved equipment. Do not bypass required grounding or electrical protection. Expected outcome: Correct facility power is available at the equipment connection.

steps.title: 5. Check for Facility Electrical Events
steps.instructions: Determine whether there was: Breaker activity Emergency-power transfer Planned electrical work Generator testing Local outage Simultaneous reset of nearby equipment Coordinate with Facilities when the problem may originate upstream. Expected outcome: Facility electrical causes are either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Inspect External Ventilation and Environment
steps.instructions: Check that external ventilation openings are unobstructed and that the sterilizer is not exposed to excessive heat, liquid, or environmental conditions that could affect operation. Expected outcome: The equipment environment is normal and external airflow is unobstructed.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Normal Startup
steps.instructions: If safe and no active cycle remains, power the sterilizer on using the normal procedure. Observe: Startup behavior Display operation Unusual sounds Unexpected shutdown Repeated restart Abnormal odor or heat Expected outcome: The system completes startup without interruption.

steps.title: 8. Stop Immediately for Electrical Warning Signs
steps.instructions: Remove the sterilizer from service if there is: Burning odor Smoke Arcing Excessive heat Repeated breaker trip Repeated spontaneous restart Visible electrical damage Do not repeatedly energize equipment showing these symptoms. Expected outcome: A potentially unsafe electrical condition is contained.

steps.title: 9. Perform Controlled Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If an external facility-power issue was corrected and the sterilizer now operates normally, complete the required functional and approved cycle verification before return to service. Expected outcome: The sterilizer remains powered throughout a complete verification cycle without restarting. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Power or Restart Problems
steps.instructions: If correct facility power is present but the sterilizer will not power on or continues restarting, remove it from service. Expected outcome: Qualified service evaluates the internal power, control, or electrical systems.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD NX unexpectedly restarted during a cycle and the load did not complete processing.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an intermittent facility receptacle supplying the sterilizer while the equipment operated normally from a verified power source.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the affected receptacle from use, coordinated repair with Facilities, verified stable sterilizer operation through an approved cycle, and returned the sterilizer to service.

helpfulDetails: Odor, heat, smoke, or electrical damage

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Touchscreen or Operator Panel Freezes During Load Setup
description: Troubleshoot frozen, delayed, or unresponsive operator controls caused by temporary software state, contamination, external input devices, power instability, or control-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not start or continue a clinical sterilization cycle if operator controls are unreliable. If the freeze occurs during an active cycle, do not interrupt the cycle unless required for safety or directed by approved procedures. Expected outcome: The sterilizer is not used when operators cannot reliably control or verify its status.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Control Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The entire touchscreen is frozen Only one area is unresponsive The display changes but touch input does not The system is simply slow The freeze happens on one setup screen Physical controls are also affected Expected outcome: Display failure, touch-input failure, and software delay are distinguished.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Screen and Panel
steps.instructions: Check for: Moisture Cleaning residue Adhesive Protective material interfering with touch Physical damage Cracks Objects resting against the screen Clean only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: The control surface is clean, dry, unobstructed, and physically intact.

steps.title: 4. Remove External Input Interference
steps.instructions: If an external scanner or other supported input accessory is connected, inspect its cable and determine whether the freeze occurs with that accessory disconnected when safe and permitted. Expected outcome: An external accessory is either ruled out or identified as contributing to the problem.

steps.title: 5. Verify Stable AC Power
steps.instructions: Check the sterilizer's power source and determine whether the complaint followed a power disturbance, building work, or unexpected restart. Expected outcome: Stable power is present.

steps.title: 6. Allow the System to Complete Current Processing
steps.instructions: If the interface appears temporarily busy during a legitimate system operation, avoid repeated inputs and observe whether normal response returns. Expected outcome: The panel resumes normal operation without intervention if the condition was temporary.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart When Safe
steps.instructions: When no cycle is active and facility procedures permit, perform a normal shutdown and restart. Do not repeatedly cycle power as a workaround for recurring control freezes. Expected outcome: The sterilizer boots normally and the touchscreen responds throughout setup.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Original Workflow
steps.instructions: Navigate through the same load-setup functions that previously produced the freeze. Check multiple screen areas and normal operator functions. Expected outcome: Setup can be completed without freezing. If operation is repeatable, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 9. Verify Complete Functional Operation
steps.instructions: Before return to service, verify normal: Startup Touch response Menu navigation Cycle selection Load setup Status display Approved cycle operation Expected outcome: Operator controls remain responsive through normal use.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent Freezing
steps.instructions: If the touchscreen repeatedly freezes, restarts, loses input, or becomes unreliable, remove the sterilizer from service. Expected outcome: Qualified service evaluates the display, touch interface, software, power supply, or control system.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD NX touchscreen stopped responding during load setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found cleaning residue on the touchscreen surface and confirmed normal system operation after the panel was properly cleaned and dried.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned the touchscreen according to approved procedures, verified normal response through repeated load setup and an approved functional check, and returned the sterilizer to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether display or touch input failed
Whether fault repeats at same screen

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Vacuum, Injection, Diffusion, or Plasma Phase Cancels
description: Troubleshoot repeat cycle cancellations during vacuum, sterilant delivery, diffusion, or plasma phases caused by load, packaging, consumables, chamber, or utility conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Sterility Assurance
steps.instructions: Treat every canceled sterilization cycle as unsuccessful unless the system and facility procedures explicitly establish otherwise. Do not release the load for patient use. Route instruments through another validated sterilization process or verified sterilizer. Expected outcome: Instruments from the canceled cycle remain segregated and patient care continues through an approved alternative.

steps.title: 2. Capture the Exact Cancellation Point
steps.instructions: Record: Displayed message Phase when cancellation occurred Whether the cancellation happens at the same phase repeatedly Load contents Cycle selected Whether the unit previously completed cycles normally Do not clear useful information before documenting it. Expected outcome: The cancellation is characterized well enough to determine whether it follows the load, consumables, or sterilizer.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Load and Packaging
steps.instructions: Check for externally verifiable load problems such as: Excessive load density Items positioned against the chamber Incorrectly arranged trays Damaged packaging Restricted openings or channels Visible moisture Materials or packaging not approved for the selected process Clinical Engineering should coordinate questionable load preparation with Sterile Processing rather than altering validated processing practices. Expected outcome: The load is dry, correctly prepared, appropriately positioned, and compatible with the intended process.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Chamber and Door Area
steps.instructions: With the system safe and idle, inspect accessible areas for: Debris Packaging trapped near the door Visible contamination Obstruction around the chamber opening Obvious seal damage visible without disassembly Expected outcome: The chamber opening and accessible sealing surfaces are clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Verify Sterilant Cassette Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm that an approved cassette is recognized, properly installed, undamaged, and shows usable capacity. Do not attempt to reuse, refill, repair, or modify a questionable cassette. Expected outcome: The sterilant source is recognized and available for the requested cycle.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Controlled Load
steps.instructions: If facility procedures allow, evaluate the sterilizer using a properly prepared controlled or routine load known to process successfully. This helps distinguish a load-related cancellation from a sterilizer-related problem. Expected outcome: A controlled load proceeds normally. If the original load configuration caused the cancellation, correct the processing issue and stop troubleshooting after successful verification.

steps.title: 7. Check Environmental and Utility Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that the sterilizer has stable electrical power and that required facility utilities and environmental conditions have not been interrupted or altered. Check for recent: Power disturbances Facility work Utility interruptions Room environmental changes Relocation or service activity Do not alter facility utilities or manufacturer configurations without authorization. Expected outcome: No external facility condition explains the phase cancellation.

steps.title: 8. Observe for Abnormal External Behavior
steps.instructions: During an approved test cycle, observe externally for: Unusual pump noise Repeated pauses Unexpected restart Door or chamber abnormalities Recurrent cancellation at the same phase Do not bypass interlocks or operate with covers removed. Expected outcome: The sterilizer progresses normally without abnormal external behavior.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Cycle Verification
steps.instructions: If the suspected external cause is corrected, complete the facility-required test or verification process before releasing the sterilizer for routine use. Expected outcome: A complete cycle finishes normally with the expected cycle record and required quality indicators. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeat Phase Cancellations
steps.instructions: If cancellations recur with correctly prepared loads, recognized consumables, stable utilities, and no accessible obstruction, remove the sterilizer from service. Expected outcome: Further investigation is transferred to qualified service personnel.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD NX repeatedly canceled during processing before completing the sterilization cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found visible moisture in the prepared load, while the sterilizer completed an approved verification cycle with a properly dry load.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the wet load from processing, coordinated load correction with Sterile Processing, verified a complete successful cycle, and returned the sterilizer to service.

title: Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) STERRAD NX Sterilizer - Vacuum Pump Is Noisy, Slow, or Unable to Reach Target Pressure
description: Troubleshoot abnormal vacuum performance by checking load, chamber, door sealing, environment, power, external airflow, and repeatability before service-level evaluation.

steps.title: 1. Protect Sterility Assurance
steps.instructions: If vacuum performance is unreliable or cycles are canceling, stop routine instrument processing on the affected sterilizer and redirect loads to verified equipment. Expected outcome: No load is released from a cycle with questionable vacuum performance.

steps.title: 2. Characterize the Vacuum Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the sterilizer: Sounds louder than normal Takes unusually long during vacuum phases Cancels during vacuum Operates intermittently Shows the problem only with certain loads Record any displayed message without assuming the pump itself is defective. Expected outcome: The vacuum symptom is documented objectively.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Load
steps.instructions: Check for: Overloading Incorrect placement Packaging against the chamber Moisture Items that may interfere with evacuation Loads that differ significantly from those previously processed successfully Expected outcome: The load is correctly prepared and arranged.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Chamber and Door Areas
steps.instructions: With the unit safe and idle, inspect accessible areas for: Debris Packaging fragments Visible contamination Material interfering with the door seal Obvious seal abnormalities Expected outcome: The chamber opening is clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Verify Stable Electrical Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that the sterilizer is connected to its intended power source and that there is no evidence of intermittent power, loose external connection, or recent electrical disturbance. Expected outcome: The sterilizer has stable facility power.

steps.title: 6. Check Accessible Ventilation Areas
steps.instructions: Inspect external ventilation openings for obvious blockage, accumulated material, or objects restricting airflow. Do not remove panels or access internal pump components. Expected outcome: External ventilation is unobstructed.

steps.title: 7. Compare Empty or Controlled Testing
steps.instructions: When approved by facility procedures, compare vacuum behavior using an appropriate controlled verification condition rather than the suspect clinical load. Listen for major changes in sound and observe whether the cancellation repeats. Expected outcome: Normal behavior with a controlled test points toward load-related conditions. Persistent abnormal behavior points toward the sterilizer.

steps.title: 8. Stop for Significant Mechanical Symptoms
steps.instructions: Immediately discontinue testing if there is: Grinding Severe vibration Smoke Burning odor Fluid leakage Excessive heat Repeated electrical reset Expected outcome: Potential equipment damage or safety risk is not worsened through repeated operation.

steps.title: 9. Verify Operation After External Correction
steps.instructions: If an obstruction, load issue, or external environmental cause is corrected, perform the required verification cycle. Expected outcome: Vacuum phases proceed normally without abnormal noise or cancellation. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Vacuum Problems
steps.instructions: If abnormal noise, slow evacuation, or vacuum-phase cancellation continues with proper loads and no external obstruction, remove the sterilizer from service. Expected outcome: Qualified service evaluates the vacuum system using manufacturer-approved procedures.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the STERRAD NX became unusually loud during the vacuum phase and repeatedly canceled cycles.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering confirmed abnormal vacuum noise and cancellation with a controlled load after external obstructions and load conditions were ruled out.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the sterilizer from service, labeled it Out of Service, and referred it for qualified vacuum-system evaluation before return-to-service testing.

helpfulDetails: Presence of odor, heat, or vibration
